thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach for customer 'Horizon Labs' on hosted cluster eu-west-1. Current p99=2.9s (SLO 2.0s), p95=1.1s. Increased streaming stalls observed. Paging oncall: @mike 

Dana: acked. I'm oncall. Jumping in. Any obvious deploys? :eyes: 

Mike: no recent deploys flagged by deploy-bot. I see a surge from a single tenant (Horizon) — traffic up 6x in last 7m. Concurrent streams ~480 (typical 80). Pattern: many long-prefix prompts + repeated function/tool calling.

deploy-bot: recent rollout: none to inference-runtime in the last 24h.

Jamie: adding SRE context — we saw similar symptoms when KV cache thrash happens due to many unique prefixes + large context windows. Streaming stalls show up as TCP-level stalls and request requeues.

Priya: monitoring graphs: attached quick snapshot (paste):
```
- cluster eu-west-1
- active workers: 64 -> worker cpu ~93%
- avg seq len: 1800 tokens for Horizon vs 220 baseline
- KV cache miss rate: 76% (baseline 12%)
- batch wait: 120ms -> 450ms
- tail latency p99: 2.9s
```

Alex-CustEng: Horizon reported increased usage after internal load test. They expect sustained higher concurrency for a feature rollout. They said requests include large system messages + iterative tool calls. 

Dana: triage plan: 1) put Horizon on emergency routing to a fallback model variant with smaller context/quantization-friendly profile; 2) enable temporary autoscale bump for eu-west-1 GPU pool for dedicated tenants; 3) apply KV cache TTL tuning / prefix hashing mitigation if quick. 

Mike: routing policy check: we have a model variant 'gpt-medium-lowlat' compatible with Horizon. Can do route override at infra layer for their tenant id. Will that impact quality? Alex-CustEng: small drop acceptable for now.

Jamie: steps to implement routing override:
```
1) run: curl -X POST https://infra.redwood.internal/route/override -d '{"tenant":"horizon","model":"gpt-medium-lowlat","expires":"+15m"}' 
2) watch route-audit logs: /var/log/routing/audit.log | tail -n 50
```

Mike: executing step 1 now.

Mike: done — route override applied. deploy-bot: recorded route change id r-13579.

Priya: watching metrics — within 90s we see batch wait drop to 210ms, KV miss rate down to 48%. p99 dropped to 1.8s — below SLO. :tada:

Dana: excellent. Keep route override for 30m while we stabilize. Next: temporary pool autoscale? We can spin 16 extra workers in eu-west-1, but spinning may take 3-4m. Do we need it?

Alex-CustEng: Horizon prefers not to increase cost yet — they'd like to keep fallback route until they finish the internal rollout.

Jamie: recommendation: keep fallback route + schedule a short runbook for Horizon to reduce prompt lengths and batch calls. Post-incident: work with CustEng to add prefix normalization at the proxy to reduce unique prefixes.

Dana: agree. I'll leave route override for 30m and monitor for regressions. Oncall-> SRE handoff: Mike, will you own quick postmortem actions (metrics, root cause hypothesis) and tag eng-runtime if needed?

Mike: taking ownership. Immediate next steps: collect flamegraphs of workers serving Horizon for last 10m, capture KV cache eviction traces, and confirm no infra-level throttles.

Priya: I pushed a helper dashboard with Horizon filters: https://grafana.redwood/1489/horizon-latency. Added alerts to page if p99 > 2.2s for 3m.

Dana: Incident timeline note:
- 1777777777 oncall-bot alerted p99 breach
- 1777777780 mike acked and triaged
- 1777777785 route override applied
- 1777777792 p99 back under SLO

Alex-CustEng: customer update sent: "We've detected elevated latency; temporarily routing your traffic to a lower-latency model variant. No data loss. Engineering is investigating optimizations."

Mike: debug snippets I'm capturing:
```
# sample worker stackcounts (top functions)
1 get_kv_block
2 apply_attention_kernels
3 serialize_stream_chunk
# kv eviction log snippet
[2026-05-22T12:31:02Z] tenant=horizon evict=42 total=1389
```

Jamie: Interesting — get_kv_block dominating suggests a high churn in KV cache. Likely cause: large, slightly-different system messages per request (user id + timestamp embedded) leading to cache fragmentation.

Priya: adding proposed mitigations for postmortem: 
- Proxy-level prefix normalization to strip non-deterministic metadata.
- Encourage Horizon to shift metadata to separate tool call payloads rather than system prompt.
- Persistence for hot prefixes for dedicated tenants (pin top-k prefixes in local cache).

Dana: agree. Action items assigned: Mike (postmortem + traces), Jamie (KV cache mitigation design + perf estimation), Priya (alert tuning + dashboard), Alex-CustEng (coordinate with Horizon for prompt changes).

Mike: will produce postmortem draft in #postmortems within 48h. Tagging eng-runtime for kernel-level optimization review: @eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: route override will auto-expire at +30m (177778 - approx).

Dana: closing loop — keeping the incident channel open for 30m monitoring. If p99 stays stable, we'll mark as mitigated and start RCA. Thanks all. :heart: 

Priya: p99 now steady ~1.7s for 5 consecutive windows. No further alerts.

Dana: marking mitigated. Will post full incident summary and link to postmortem when available.

Alex-CustEng: Horizon confirms reduced latency on their side. They will delay their roll until we confirm prefix-normalization changes. Thanks team.

mike: end of thread notes: root cause hypothesis = high concurrency from single-tenant with high unique-prefix rate => KV cache thrash causing batching inefficiency and streaming stalls. Mitigation successful by routing to lower-context model; long-term fix = proxy normalization + pinning hot prefixes + eval of kv cache TTL heuristics.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved. :white_check_mark:
